title: SWHAP validation report (v1)
description: Machine-readable report emitted by swhap-validate / check_swhap.sh. Status: DRAFT pending W1 sign-off. Prose contract: specs/validator-report.md (semantics: exit mapping, determinism, versioning); this schema governs shape. schema_version is the constant "1" for the entire v1.x line; additive (minor) evolution keeps the open content model, so consumers MUST be tolerant readers. Canonical serialization: UTF-8, LF, one trailing newline, 2-space indent, keys sorted byte-wise, findings sorted by id.

schema_version.description: Major schema version. Constant "1" for every v1.x report; consumers route on this value only.

findings.description: All FAIL/WARN/INFO findings. Passing checks emit no finding (they are counted in summary.pass and listed in run.checks_run). MUST be sorted by id, ascending byte-wise.

tool.description: Producer identification. Build-stable, never run-variant: part of the canonical (byte-comparable) output.

commit.description: Git commit of the validator build, when built from a checkout.

run.description: Run context. The run-variant field set is EXACTLY {timestamp, repo, invocation}: the only fields in the whole document allowed to carry wall-clock time or machine-/invocation-specific data (D4 determinism). Under --run-meta-stable these are absent and meta_stable is true; the M4 AI-on/off non-interference proof byte-compares such reports.

timestamp.description: Run wall-clock time, RFC 3339 UTC second precision with Z suffix. The only clock read in the report. Run-variant: absent under meta_stable.

meta_stable.description: True iff emitted with --run-meta-stable (run-variant fields omitted).

profile.description: Validation profile (validator plan section 4.2). legacy = D2/C3 read-only audit: findings keep true severities but are enforced:false, so the exit code is 0 unless the tool itself errs (exit 2/3/4).

gate.description: Gate context; in v1 only LG-1 is gate-sensitive (FAIL at publish, WARN at build). The publish step hard-requires exit 0 at gate=publish.

strict_warn.description: True iff --strict-warn was given (enforced WARN findings then force exit 1).

repo.description: Repository path or URL as invoked. Run-variant: absent under meta_stable.

head.description: Commit hash examined (SHA-1 or SHA-256 repo). Content-derived, NOT run-variant: stays in canonical output (its equality across AI-on/off runs is itself non-interference evidence). Required in practice for exit-0/1 reports; may be absent in partial error reports.

refs_checked.description: Fully-qualified refs examined, sorted byte-wise ascending.

invocation.description: argv echo for audit trails. Run-variant: absent under meta_stable.

checks_run.description: Every check ID executed, sorted byte-wise ascending. Load-bearing for the M4 proof: identical checks_run proves the same battery ran on both sides.

checks_skipped.description: Checks not executed (--skip, profile/gate exclusion, or unavailability such as RB-1 without swhap-core) — skipped is always reported, never silent. Sorted by id. Reasons come from a fixed vocabulary: deterministic, no paths or timestamps.

then.description: meta-stable mode: run-variant fields must be ABSENT (not null, not empty).

summary.description: fail/warn/info count FINDINGS; pass counts EXECUTED CHECKS that emitted zero findings (mixed semantics, deliberate and frozen). exit_code MUST equal the process exit code (pre-D1 dual mode: each per-profile document carries its own profile's code; the process exits with the max).

exit_code.description: 0 pass | 1 enforced FAIL (or enforced WARN under --strict-warn) | 2 usage/config error | 3 internal tool error | 4 precondition unmet (any PC-* FAIL; shallow clone is 4, not 2). Exact total mapping rule: prose contract section 4.1 (precedence 2 then 3 then 4 then 1 then 0; counts never matter; state never enters). Reports with 2/3/4 are non-certifying.

id.description: Stable finding identifier: <check_id> + ':' + first 12 lowercase-hex chars of SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the finding's SUBJECT (the registered subject-key projection of `object`, NOT the whole object — prose contract section 2.1). Durable across reruns over identical inputs AND across v1.x tool upgrades (adding non-subject object keys is minor and id-preserving; changing the subject-key set is a major event). Unique within a report (collision = internal error, exit 3). AI explain/ keys per-finding explanations by this id; intake task-lists key on it. The family prefix matches the relaxed checkId pattern so a vendored v1.0 schema still validates a v1.x finding from a new check family.

severity.description: Intrinsic classification under the active profile+gate. CLOSED enum for the whole v1 line (the exit mapping quantifies over it). Never downgraded to express non-enforcement — that is `enforced`. Legacy profile keeps true severities (CM-2 stays FAIL-classified). Gate-dependent severity is legitimate (LG-1: FAIL at publish, WARN at build).

enforced.description: Whether this finding participates in exit-code computation. Strict profiles: true. Legacy profile: false for every finding except PC-* — the truthful representation of report-only mode (severity tells the truth about the artifact, enforced about the run's posture, the exit code follows mechanically).

object.description: Check-specific machine data. MUST be deterministic (no wall-clock, no absolute paths — repo-relative POSIX only, no hostnames/PIDs/durations). The registered subject-key subset uniquely identifies the finding's subject within its check and seeds the finding id; non-subject keys may be added in minor versions without re-keying. Common key names: tag, ref, path, row, field, expected, actual, size_bytes, threshold_bytes, item. EVERY string value derived from untrusted archive/CSV bytes MUST use the byte-safe encoding (prose section 2.5a): non-UTF-8 bytes and ALL control/ANSI bytes are rendered as \xHH text, never emitted raw — applies to ANY check (CSV-2, CSV-6, BP-4...), not just PI-1. PERSONAL-DATA RULE (all checks, not only PI-1): no finding may place a literal personal email address in object/messages/remediation; it carries the redacted token {value_hmac12, domain_class, domain?} of prose section 2.5b.

message_plain.description: Plain-language explanation. Audience tag: non-expert (Profile A) — x-audience: non-expert. Self-contained, no git/CLI knowledge assumed; texts reviewed by a real non-expert at M1b. Intake's Profile-A rendering uses only this field plus severity, required_approver_role, state, remediation. Subject to the byte-safe / control-char-free / personal-data rules (prose sections 2.5a/2.5b); markup-surface (markdown/HTML) escaping is the RENDERING CONSUMER's responsibility, not the producer's.

message_technical.description: Technical detail. Audience tag: expert (Profiles B/D, curators, CI logs) — x-audience: expert. Same byte-safe / control-char-free / personal-data rules as message_plain (prose sections 2.5a/2.5b).

required_approver_role.description: Role that must approve/resolve this finding (crit-M11). OPEN enum across v1.x (a deeper M2 legal model extends it additively, e.g. data-protection-officer). The enum branch below is ADVISORY (the documented v1 values, kept as an annotation); the schema accepts ANY non-empty string so a vendored v1.0 schema still validates a v1.x report that introduces a new role. Consumers MUST treat an unrecognized value as the most restrictive known role (legal-curator). user-provided input never satisfies a legal-curator item (crit-M10).

state.description: Approval state — a DERIVED VIEW computed at run time from the journal ledger via the finding-state derivation function (prose contract section 2.8: the latest state-transition ledger entry whose details.machine == 'finding:'+id). The ledger is canonical; the report is never written back. `open` when no such entry exists (legacy repos, pre-M1c runs). OPEN enum across v1.x: the enum branch below is ADVISORY (documented v1 values); the schema accepts ANY non-empty string so a vendored v1.0 schema still validates. Consumers treat unknown values as open. state never feeds the exit-code computation (no approval-as-bypass); only checks that themselves read the ledger (LG-1) react to approvals.

provenance.description: Provenance-state reference for the metadata item this finding is about. REQUIRED on LG-1 findings and on CSV-3 findings flagging inferred/defaulted dates; optional elsewhere.

remediation.description: Actionable next step, plain language (rendered to Profile A).

checkId.description: Stable registry ID (validator plan section 2.4). Documented v1 families: PC preflight (FAIL => exit 4), TF tree fidelity, BP branch purity, CSV version-history contract, CM codemeta, SZ size/LFS, RB reproducibility, DV published divergence, JC journal coverage, LG legal gate, PI email lint. Letter suffix covers staged forms (JC-1a). ADDING A NEW CHECK FAMILY IS A MINOR EVENT: the pattern accepts any 2-5 uppercase-letter family prefix so a vendored v1.0 schema still validates a v1.x report from a later family (e.g. a M2 legal family LM-1). Renames/removals of an existing ID are major schema events; retired IDs are reserved forever; changed semantics means a new ID.

error.description: Present on best-effort reports for exit 2 (usage) or 3 (internal). Such reports are non-certifying.
